html:
The Filipino writer, doctor and reformer whose novels exposed Spanish rule and whose execution in 1896 made him the national hero of the Philippines.

Born in Calamba to a well-off family, Rizal studied in Manila and then in Madrid, Paris and Heidelberg, training as an eye doctor. In Europe he joined the Propaganda Movement, Filipinos who asked Spain for reform: equal rights, a free press and limits on the power of the friars.

His novel Noli Me Tángere (1887) showed colonial abuse through the story of a young man returning from Europe. Its darker sequel, El filibusterismo (1891), went further. Both were banned in the colony.

Back home in 1892 he founded a reform society and was at once exiled to Dapitan on Mindanao. He never joined the armed Katipunan, but when it rose in 1896 the Spanish arrested him. He was shot in Manila on 30 December 1896. His death fired the Philippine Revolution and made his name its banner.
sum: The Filipino writer, doctor and reformer whose novels exposed Spanish rule and whose execution in 1896 made him the national hero of the Philippines.
